The University of Jos has appointed Prof. Patricia Mamko Lar as its Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position in the history of the institution. Prof. Lar succeeds Prof. Tanko Ishaya. According to a statement issued by the university on Thursday, “Professor Patricia Mamko Lar formally takes over from Professor Tanko Ishaya FBCS FNCS as the 11th substantive and 1st female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos.” The statement added: “Professor Patricia Lar is the 11th substantive and 1st female Vice-Chancellor of the university.” The appointment was announced on Thursday, 12th November, 2026, during a special meeting of the 15th governing council of the university. UNIJOS gets first female Vice Chancellor Eight professors jostle for UNIJOS VC position Eight professors jostle for UNIJOS VC seat “The announcement was made by Senator Grace Folashade Bent CON, Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, during the special meeting of the 15th Governing Council on Thursday, 12th November 2026,” the statement said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Presenting the letter of appointment to the new Vice-Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor charged her to be focused. The statement, signed by Emmanuel Madugu, ANIPR, Deputy Registrar, Information and Public Relations, _For: Registrar/Secretary to Council_, concluded: “Details shortly.” Prof. Lar’s appointment marks a historic milestone for the University of Jos, which was founded in 1971. A professor of Medical Microbiology at the university, Prof. Lar previously served as Acting Vice-Chancellor of the Yakubu Gowon University, Abuja, formerly the University of Abuja, for a six-month term.
